Parametric-bootstrap likelihood-ratio (and Vuong) test of nested fits

Source: R/tests_fit.R
boot_lr_test.Rd

Calibrates the comparison of a restricted fit with a fit that nests it by simulation under the restricted model: B outcome vectors are drawn from the restricted fit, both models are refit on each, and the bootstrap distribution of the likelihood-ratio statistic (and, for an mnl() versus imnl() pair, of the raw Vuong statistic) gives the p-values. This is the calibrated comparison for restrictions on the boundary of the parameter space, where neither the chi-square reference of lr_test() nor the normal reference of vuong() holds: the inflated model against the multinomial logit (\(\phi = 1\), where the split coefficients are not identified), the random-intercept model against the multinomial logit (\(\sigma = 0\)). It applies to the pairs lr_test() accepts (a subset of the parameters within one family, with the nest structure shared for the nested logit, or the multinomial logit with the same covariates inside a nested logit, an HEV, or a random-intercept fit), to the multinomial logit inside the inflated multinomial logit, and to an inflated multinomial logit inside one with more inflated alternatives; and to two nested rologit() fits of the same rankings, where few rankings per coefficient make the chi-square reference of lr_test() unreliable. Penalized fits (firth = TRUE or a prior) are refused.

Usage

boot_lr_test(restricted, full, B = 199L, cores = 1L)

Arguments

restricted, full

Two "choicemodel" fits to the same cases, the second nesting the first.

B

Number of bootstrap replicates (default 199).

cores

Number of parallel workers.

Value

A data frame of class "iia_test" with one row per statistic (LR, and Vuong for an mnl / imnl pair): the observed statistic, p.value, and p.boot. For the LR, p.value is the chi-square p-value with df degrees of freedom for an interior restriction, the (conservative) chi-square p-value for \(\sigma = 0\), the 50:50 chi-square mixture's for the mnl / imnl pair with one inflated alternative and an intercept-only split (with lr_test()'s rule: NA when the inflated fit is degenerate, its outcome coefficients diverging or at a saddle, as the method line then says), and NA for any other mnl / imnl pair, which has no valid asymptotic reference; for the Vuong statistic p.value is NA, and p.boot is one-sided in favour of the full model. The attribute "boot_statistics" holds the replicates; n_failed (dropped), n_nonconverged (replicates in which either refit did not converge; kept), and n_negative (replicates whose full refit fell short of the restricted one by more than the embedding's own gap at a boundary restriction; set to 0 and kept) are attributes too, and the method line reports each that is not zero. A few non-converged replicates are common for the inflated model on data simulated without inflation, where the split equation runs towards \(\phi = 1\) and the optimizer stops short of a maximum that is not attained; n_negative guards against an optimizer that ends above its own start and should be 0. The outcomes are drawn independently case by case (unit by unit for a random-intercept restricted fit), so the calibration assumes independent cases; with clustered data the bootstrap p-value is not calibrated. The split equation must contain an intercept named (Intercept); a constant column under another name is not recognized.

Details

Each replicate refits both models the way the original fits were obtained (the engine's own starting values and, for the inflated model, its multistart), and in addition from the original estimates and, for the full model, from the restricted replicate estimates embedded in the full model at the restriction (zero for the added coefficients, \(\lambda = 1\), scales 1, a standard deviation near zero, or the split equation at \(\phi = 1 - 10^{-8}\)). The full refit therefore cannot end below the restricted one, and the replicate statistic is maximized as thoroughly as the observed one, which is computed the same way. A replicate takes about as long as the two original fits; cores runs replicates in parallel. The outcomes, and the seeds of the ranking draws, come from the session's generator before the refits run, so a result under set.seed() does not depend on cores.

The outcomes are drawn from the restricted fit's probabilities, case by case, or for a random-intercept restricted fit unit by unit (one intercept vector per unit, then the unit's cases). Rankings are drawn as the order of the restricted fit's utilities plus independent standard Gumbel errors, cut to each case's observed pattern: the same rank groups, with the same sizes in the same order (a tie stays a tie at its positions), and the alternatives below them unranked; the truncation and the ties are thus treated as independent of the utilities.

Under separation (in mnl() and rologit() fits without unit fixed effects or inflation) the statistic compares the suprema of the two log-likelihoods, not the values where the optimizer stopped (see lr_test()); replicates whose refit is separated are kept and counted, since separation can be common under the null when the rankings or choices are few or the attributes discrete (a replicate in which an alternative is never chosen, or never ranked above another, is such a replicate). When the restricted fit is itself separated, the outcomes are drawn from the point at which its supremum is approached, where the separated comparisons are near-deterministic (the restricted model's limit), not from where its optimizer stopped. Outside that scope a replicate in which an alternative with coefficients of its own is never chosen fails. Replicates whose refit fails are dropped and counted; the p-value is \((1 + k) / (B' + 1)\) with \(B'\) the successful replicates and \(k\) the number of replicate statistics at least as large as the observed one. Frequency weights are honoured by expanding the design to one row per case (integer weights only; not with random intercepts, where a weighted unit stands for several units with their own intercepts). Fixed-effects fits are refused (the unit constants would be re-estimated on simulated outcomes that may make them unidentified).

See also

lr_test(), vuong(), boot_pvalue()

Other model comparison: classification(), compare_models(), fit_stats(), lr_test(), vuong()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(2)
d <- rmnl(400, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5)))
m0 <- mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d)
m1 <- imnl(y ~ x1 + x2 | 1, data = d)           # a constant captive share; none in the data
#> Warning: The fit is at a boundary: the split equation puts every case in one regime (the inflated model collapses onto the MNL); compare with mnl() by boot_lr_test(), or by lr_test() when the split has only an intercept.
boot_lr_test(m0, m1, B = 19)
#> Parametric bootstrap under the restricted model, 19 replicates; the LR's asymptotic p-value is the 50:50 chi-square mixture (a constant captive share) 
#>                                                   test statistic df p.value
#>   LR (parametric bootstrap under the restricted model)      0.00  1       1
#>  Vuong, raw (full vs restricted; parametric bootstrap)     -0.21 NA      NA
#>  p.boot
#>     1.0
#>     0.9
# }
